deploy-bot: Deploy finished: release v1.12.3 -> prod-usw2. Post-deploy quickchecks running. Initial summary: RPS -11.8% vs baseline, p95 +180ms, 429s up 0.6%. Kicking off 10m observation.
Suzanne: saw the dip on /v1/generate, also small tail at 1.5s. no 5xx.
Raj: any stack traces or threadpool saturations in logs?
Marta: checked pod logs, nothing obvious. connection pool WARNs around the time of the spike.
Oncall-Mike: suggest we try graceful throttling on inference pool A before rollback. reduce concurrency and measure.
Suzanne: agree. if throttling doesn't help in 10m we should pin back to v1.12.2.
Marta: change window ends in ~22m; want to avoid full rollback if possible.
Raj: can we also nudge the autoscaler policy to scale up a bit? could be warmup issue.
Marta: autoscaler already at target. scaling up will add cold starts. prefer throttling first.
Suzanne: throttling command (prod cluster):
```
kubectl set env deploy/inference-pool-a CONCURRENCY=8 -n prod
```
Suzanne: reduces per-pod concurrency from 16->8. should flatten queue spikes.
Marta: applying now, rolling env update.
deploy-bot: Received command: `kubectl set env deploy/inference-pool-a CONCURRENCY=8 -n prod` by Marta at 2930123508
deploy-bot: Rolling update started for deploy/inference-pool-a - 3 pods updated so far.
Marta: updated 3/6 pods, no restart errors.
Oncall-Mike: bouncing metrics, give it 2m after rollout completes.
Raj: watching p95, 429 rate, and qlen.
Suzanne: initial 2m window: p95 dropped from +180ms to +90ms, RPS still -9%. 429s unchanged.
Marta: full env update completed at 2930123550.
Oncall-Mike: good sign on p95, but RPS drop persists. Could be client-side backoff or prefetch change.
Raj: any traffic-splitting anomalies? release-cop can you check CDN or gateway routing?
release-cop: checked gateway logs, no route mismatch. upstream service ingress saw increased SYN retries for some pods during deploy window.
Marta: that points to a kernel-level socket reuse edge case we've seen on this instance type. we hit it at scale when concurrency decreases per-pod.
Suzanne: hmm. throttle helped latency but RPS not fully recovered. next step: gradual rollforward to increase replica count for old variant v1.12.2 while we investigate?
Oncall-Mike: option A: pin traffic back to v1.12.2 (fast but heavier). Option B: increase old variant capacity via canary backlog shift. prefer option B if we can do without breaking change window.
Marta: can do replica bump for v1.12.2 in the canary set: `kubectl scale deploy/inference-v1-12-2 --replicas=12 -n prod`
Raj: scaling old variant will increase cost but buys time.
Suzanne: agree. let's scale old variant by +6 replicas, monitor 10m. if RPS recovers, we keep and file infra bug. if not, escalate to rollback.
Marta: scaling now.
deploy-bot: `kubectl scale` executed by Marta at 2930123575. Target replicas: inference-v1-12-2 -> 12.
Marta: scaled, evenly routed via traffic-split.
Raj: metrics update: after scaling, RPS improved to -3% vs baseline, p95 ~ +60ms, 429s down slightly.
Suzanne: that's acceptable for now. we'll keep throttle and extra replicas for the next 2 hours, open a ticket for kernel socket reuse footgun.
Oncall-Mike: agree. assign to infra-team with priority P2. also add note to release notes and postmortem template.
release-cop: updated release notes: added entry "v1.12.3: Observed RPS regression on high-conn workloads; temporary mitigations applied (reduced per-pod concurrency + scaled previous variant). Investigating kernel socket reuse under specific instance types."
Marta: creating ticket INF-4826, linking logs + heatmap.
Suzanne: thanks. marking thread as monitoring. if metrics are stable at next check (2930123620) we'll close and document mitigation steps. :white_check_mark:
Oncall-Mike: I'm around if it needs rollback. otherwise hold till end of change window.
Raj: lgtm
Marta: closing temporary measures; will post longer writeup in infra board later.
deploy-bot: Post-deploy check complete: observation window ended at 2930123620. No rollback initiated.
